Manipur Shows Signs Of Recovery: Zero Cross-Firing Cases In 3 Months, Record Arms Seizures, Peace Talks
Officials credit this improvement to enhanced coordination among central forces, proactive roles by community leaders, and growing willingness of rival groups to engage in dialogue

This brings the total number of recovered weapons to 5,859. With zero exchange-of-fire cases in the last three months, record recoveries of arms, and a weakening of underground armed networks, Manipur appears to be slowly emerging from the shadow of prolonged ethnic unrest and insurgency. According to a senior official, a series of breakthroughs in peace talks, major seizures of illegal weapons, and a significant decline in violence have raised cautious hopes of a new beginning for the troubled northeastern state.
Essential items have started moving from Imphal uninterrupted and reaching all areas, a senior official said.
Recommended Stories
Over the past three months, the government of India has facilitated three rounds each of peace talks with representatives of both the Meitei and Kuki communities, historically at odds since ethnic violence erupted in mid-2023. According to senior officials, the talks have been “constructive", with all stakeholders agreeing to continue dialogue.
While joint meetings between the two communities have not yet taken place, a key shift is evident—most stakeholders from both groups are now participating in separate dialogue platforms, unlike earlier rounds, a source said. The government is hopeful about convening a joint meeting by the end of this year, a step seen as crucial for achieving lasting reconciliation.
Record Recoveries of Illegal Weapons
Following an appeal by governor Ajay Bhalla earlier this year to surrender illegal arms, 1,089 weapons have been voluntarily handed over by various groups and individuals. This brings the total number of recovered weapons to 5,859.
The most significant recoveries have occurred in the last month.
The biggest haul took place on the night of June 13-14, when Manipur police and security forces recovered 328 weapons from five districts in the Imphal Valley.
In the third-largest seizure, security forces recovered 203 weapons during operations in early July.
“From the midnight of July 3 to the morning of July 4, 2025, security forces conducted coordinated search operations across the hill districts of Tengnoupal, Kangpokpi, Chandel, and Churachandpur, acting on specific intelligence inputs. The joint teams—comprising Manipur Police, Assam Rifles, Indian Army, and Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs)—uncovered large caches of arms, ammunition, explosives, and other warlike materials from concealed locations," Manipur police said.
Crackdown on Extortion and Insurgency Networks
Security forces have intensified operations against criminal and extortion networks. To date, over 600 extortion-related cases have been registered, with more than 320 arrests made.
Dozens of underground operatives affiliated with various militant outfits have also been apprehended, signalling a systematic effort to dismantle insurgent financing and logistics chains.
Violence at a Historic Low
In a major milestone, the last three months have witnessed only one isolated firing incident and no exchange of FIRs between hostile groups—the lowest level of violence since tensions began in 2023.
Officials credit this improvement to enhanced coordination among central forces, proactive roles by community leaders, and the growing willingness of rival groups to engage in dialogue.
